The restaurant opened on a Friday. It closed fourteen months later. Chef Marco Aliende had bet everything on it. His savings. His reputation. His marriage, eventually. The food was extraordinary. Critics raved. Diners lined up. But the rent was four thousand a month. The insurance was another two thousand. The permits took eleven months. By the time he opened, he was already in debt. The pandemic did not help. Nobody's pandemic helped. Takeout kept him alive for six months. Then the landlord raised the rent. Marco fought it. He lost. The last meal he served was a Tuesday night prix fixe for twelve guests. They all cried. He did not. He said he would try again somewhere cheaper. Somewhere smaller. The restaurant industry has a seventy percent failure rate. Marco knows the number. He does not care. Some people cook because they must.
